access_model: All access to miktam-mini is remote — SSH from miktam-mbp via VS Code Remote. There is no physical console workflow for this machine.

timeline.note: backgrounded but NOT nohup'd or disowned

timeline.command: sudo pfctl -e && echo 'block out all' | sudo pfctl -f -

timeline.observed: SSH session from miktam-mbp to miktam-mini severed immediately — 'totally disconnected'
no reconnect; 90s safety-net timer did not fire (no AUTO-RESTORED message ever seen)

timeline.note: only recovery path available — no console access to run 'sudo pfctl -d' locally

root_cause_of_failed_self_heal: The armed background job (sleep 90 && sudo pfctl -d) was not nohup'd or disowned. When the parent SSH session died (as a direct effect of the block it had just applied), the job almost certainly received SIGHUP and was killed before its 90s elapsed — so it never ran pfctl -d.
methodological_gap: The pre-registered S3 protocol assumes an operator can still probe the machine locally during the outage ('confirm SQLite corpus still readable', 're-run search_properties') to verify inference keeps working while only outbound-dependent operations fail. Because ALL access to this machine is remote (SSH from mbp, no physical console), a full outbound block also severs the only channel available to run those checks. The test cannot distinguish 'inference still works locally' from 'we have no way to find out' — those checks were never executed during the actual outage window, only before and after (post-reboot).

recovery.commands_needed: not applicable — no remote command could reach the machine to apply a targeted fix
recovery.note: confirms exp_020's LaunchDaemon setup survives a full reboot cleanly, independent of this test's actual purpose

verdict: INCONCLUSIVE as pre-registered — not because the architecture failed, but because the pre-registration didn't account for the access model. What IS confirmed: corpus/model state survived the outage + reboot with zero data loss, and Ollama's LaunchDaemon self-recovers on boot with no manual re-enrichment. What is NOT confirmed: whether local inference kept working during the outage itself, since there was no way to observe it without network access.
real_world_cost: One unplanned reboot of the production inference machine; ~5 minutes of unavailability from disconnect to confirmed recovery.
